questions.text: Should the opening invocation be visualized only as typography cards, or should we include illustrative establishing shots of Chandrabhaga river bank and Lord Pandurang?
Is the narrator (Sant Dasganu Maharaj) ever shown on screen in this chapter, or is his voice purely off-screen narration?
What is the approved visual style for the typography cards (font, color, background) beyond 'flat-colour style'?
Where exactly does the initial eating and instruction take place? Malin's house, Shiva temple, or Bankatlal's house?
What is the visual appearance of Shri Gajanan Maharaj (clothing, hair, accessories) as per canonical description?
What is the visual appearance of Pitambar Shimpi (age, clothing, distinguishing features)?
Does the miracle show the hollow forming dynamically, or only the result (tumba submerged)?
Is Bankatlal present during this scene, or only Pitambar and Maharaj?
What time of day is it? The lighting direction affects shadows and mood.
What is the exact size and shape of the tumba? Is it a typical bottle gourd shape?
What is the exact architectural layout of Manik Chowk at sunset (shop positions, central feature)?
Should the cowherd be visually distinct or remain a generic background figure?
How many shopkeepers are visible lighting lamps, and what are their specific actions?
What is Bhavaniram's exact attire and physical details (e.g., beard length, shawl color)?
How should the metaphorical 'sun of wisdom' be visually suggested in the Manik Chowk establishing shot?
What is the exact visual appearance of Ichharam Shetji (age, clothing, distinguishing features like rudraksha, vibhuti)?
How should the transformation of Bankatlal's house into Dwarka be depicted visually (architectural details, signage, symbolic elements)?
What specific naivedya items are offered beyond 'various' for accurate depiction (e.g., specific sweets, fruits)?
Is there a specific color palette or line weight for the approved flat-colour style beyond the general description?
Should the narrator's voice be heard over all shots, or only for the narration lines (S9-L1 to S9-L9)?
Should the visual of Maharaj as Vitthal standing on a brick (Ovi 138) be a direct depiction or a symbolic representation?
For the author's humility shot (Ovi 142-143), what specific imagery does the owner prefer: Dasganu as an insect, or Dasganu as a small devotee before Maharaj?
The cattle watering trough (hal) is mentioned in Ovi 144. Should we show Maharaj sitting at the trough or just the trough with water?
For the chilim shot (Ovi 146), should we show Maharaj's face or only hands?
The closing prayer (Ovi 147-148) uses a bowing prayer preset. Is the folded hands gesture sufficient, or should we include a book or manuscript representing the text?
